idiom_name: express-session plus @types/express-session declaration merging for typed session data
implementation_notes: The runtime realization is the same as JavaScript - express-session with a compatible server-side store - but TypeScript changes the contract surface: express-session ships no type definitions of its own, so the project installs the DefinitelyTyped package @types/express-session and augments the SessionData interface (declare module 'express-session' { interface SessionData { cart?: Cart } }) to make req.session.cart compile-time checked. Store choice, cookie attributes, expiry and failure behaviour remain runtime concerns; the types only stop the access path from silently drifting. Framework alternatives (NestJS wrapping express-session, Fastify session plugins) keep the same shape: middleware plus an external store.
pitfalls: Without the types package SessionData stays an untyped bag and typos in session keys compile happily; with declaration merging in a file that is not part of the program, the augmentation silently does not apply.

The middleware order matters as much as in JavaScript - session must be registered before the routes that use it - and a typed handler does not protect against a record written by an older deployment.
TypeScript types also do not constrain the serialized record: the store still holds JSON written by whichever version ran before, so a version field is what actually protects the session shape.
